[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Peace of Westphalia was a series of peace treaties signed in 1648 that marked the end of the Thirty Years' War in Europe.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The peace talks took place in the cities of Münster and Osnabrück, in modern-day Germany.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Thirty Years' War began in 1618 in the Holy Roman Empire, sparked by a religious dispute between Catholics and Protestants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The war lasted for thirty years and involved major powers such as France, Sweden, and Spain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Peace of Westphalia established the principle of state sovereignty, allowing each state to control its own affairs without outside interference.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Peace of Westphalia helped to end religious wars in Europe and paved the way for religious tolerance and freedom of worship.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It established the concept of international law and a system for resolving conflicts through diplomacy and negotiation.
